# Summary

This post documents the full research plan for applying RAM WNNs to network intrusion detection. We surveyed the literature, identified benchmarks to beat, and designed an implementation roadmap that leverages the existing infrastructure from our language modeling work.

# Literature Survey

## WNN for IDS --- Prior Art

Three lines of work directly inform our approach:

**FWIW** [@susskind2023fwiw]: The closest predecessor. Deploys a weightless neural network on FPGA for binary classification (normal vs attack) on UNSW-NB15, achieving **98.5% accuracy with only 192 bytes** of model parameters. Uses 59$\times$ fewer LUTs and 1.6$\times$ higher throughput than LogicNets [@umuroglu2020logicnets]. Open-source at `github.com/ZSusskind/FWIW`.

**BTHOWeN** [@susskind2022bthowen]: Introduces Bloom filter-based discriminators with Gaussian thermometer encoding. Achieves 41% error reduction over BloomWiSARD and 51% model size reduction. Full SystemVerilog RTL is open-source at `github.com/ZSusskind/BTHOWeN`. Not tested on IDS datasets, but the architecture is directly applicable.

**DWN** [@bacellar2024dwn]: Differentiable Weightless Neural Networks trained via a novel Extended Finite Difference technique. Achieves average rank 2.5 on tabular benchmarks (vs XGBoost's 3.5), with 2522$\times$ improvement in energy-delay product over FINN. Open-source at `github.com/alanbacellar/DWN`. Also not tested on IDS, but provides a powerful training alternative to our GA/TS approach.

A WiSARD-based IDS paper (IDC 2021, Springer) tested WiSARD on CICIDS2017 for DDoS and PortScan detection, reporting competitive results with significantly lower time complexity.

## Feature Encoding for WNNs

Converting continuous network features to binary RAM inputs is critical. Three encoding strategies exist:

1. **Linear thermometer**: Uniform threshold spacing. Simple but wasteful for skewed distributions (e.g., packet sizes follow heavy-tailed distributions).

2. **Gaussian thermometer** [@susskind2022bthowen]: Thresholds placed according to Gaussian CDF. More bits encode the dense center. 40%+ error reduction over linear.

3. **Distributive thermometer** [@bacellar2022distributive]: Distribution-adaptive encoding with no distributional assumptions. Up to 26.3% accuracy gain when distributions are non-Gaussian. Recommended for network features since packet statistics are typically heavy-tailed.

For UNSW-NB15's 49 features with 4--8 bits each, we expect ~300--400 binary input bits per flow.

## Commercial Landscape

The NDR (Network Detection and Response) market is projected at \$5.8B by 2030 (9.6% CAGR). Major vendors (Darktrace, Vectra AI, ExtraHop, Corelight) use proprietary ML but none use WNN/lookup-table approaches --- this is purely academic so far.

Key commercial insight: existing products cost \$55K--350K+/year. A WNN-on-FPGA approach could offer comparable detection at a fraction of the cost, with the unique advantage of inspecting *every* packet rather than sampling.

# Datasets

## Primary: UNSW-NB15

Selected because most FPGA IDS papers use it, enabling direct comparison.

- **Source**: University of New South Wales [@moustafa2015unswnb15]
- **Samples**: 175,341 train / 82,332 test (standard split from 2.5M total)
- **Features**: 49 (integer, float, binary, nominal, timestamp)
- **Classes**: 10 (Normal + Fuzzers, Analysis, Backdoors, DoS, Exploits, Generic, Reconnaissance, Shellcode, Worms)
- **Binary split**: Normal (87%) vs Attack (13%)
- **Known issues**: Severe within-class imbalance (Worms = 0.0008% of records)

## Secondary

| Dataset | Samples | Features | Classes | Role |
|---------|---------|----------|---------|------|
| CICIDS2017 [@sharafaldin2018cicids2017] | 2.8M | 78 | 15 | Cross-validation, modern attacks |
| NSL-KDD [@tavallaee2009nslkdd] | 126K / 23K | 41 | 5 | Classic benchmark, concept drift (test has 14 novel attack types) |
| CICIoT2023 | Large | 47 | 33 | IoT-specific (bridges to edge AI) |

## Feature Engineering Plan

| Feature type | Examples | Encoding | Bits |
|-------------|---------|----------|------|
| Numerical (continuous) | duration, sbytes, dbytes, rate | Distributive thermometer | 4--8 per feature |
| Numerical (discrete) | sport, dsport, ct\_srv\_src | Thermometer or binary | 4--8 per feature |
| Categorical | proto, service, state | One-hot or direct binary | 2--4 per feature |
| Binary flags | land, logged\_in, is\_host\_login | Pass-through | 1 per feature |
| **Total estimated** | | | **~300--400 bits** |

: Proposed encoding for UNSW-NB15 features. {#tbl-encoding}

# Research Contributions

We identify four novel contributions, none of which exist in the current literature:

## 1. Multi-Class WNN IDS

All WNN IDS work does binary classification only (normal vs attack). We will be the first to classify attack *type* (10 classes on UNSW-NB15). Our multi-stage architecture (S0 predicts category, S1 predicts specific attack) maps naturally to this problem.

## 2. GA/TS-Optimized Connectivity for IDS

No IDS paper uses evolutionary connectivity optimization. Our [phased search](../optimization-methods.qmd#phased-search) (coarse GA $\rightarrow$ fine TS) can discover which feature subsets are most discriminative for each attack type --- essentially automated feature selection at the neuron level.

## 3. Online Adaptive IDS

WiSARD's inherent incremental learning (bit-set = train, bit-clear = untrain) enables real-time concept drift adaptation. This is uniquely powerful for IDS where new attack patterns emerge daily. No WNN IDS paper has demonstrated this capability.

## 4. Cross-Dataset Generalization

We will train on UNSW-NB15 and evaluate on CICIDS2017 (and vice versa), measuring generalization gap. Prior work shows 96.1% $\rightarrow$ 88.4% degradation for traditional ML when transferring between datasets. Can GA/TS-optimized connectivity find more generalizable features?

# Benchmarks to Beat

::: {.callout-important}
## Standard vs Random Split

The evaluation protocol matters enormously. The standard temporal split (175K train / 82K test) is **12 points harder** than random 90/10 splits due to temporal shift, class distribution differences, and 30% duplicate leakage in the full dataset. All our primary goals target the **standard split** --- the realistic deployment scenario. See [Week 18](20260323-week18.qmd) for the full analysis.
:::

## Standard Split Goals (Primary --- Realistic Deployment)

Literature baselines on the standard temporal split (from [@zoghi2024ids; @springeropen2020unswnb15; @mdpi2024enhanced]):

| Method | Accuracy | F1-Macro | FPR | Source |
|--------|----------|----------|-----|--------|
| Random Forest | 87.2% | ~87% | ~12% | Our reproduction (Week 18) |
| XGBoost | 87.3% | ~87% | ~12% | Our reproduction (Week 18) |
| SVM | ~86% | ~85% | ~15% | [@springeropen2020unswnb15] |
| DNN (sequential) | ~88% | ~87% | ~10% | [@zoghi2024ids] |
| BiLSTM (deep learning) | ~89% | ~89% | ~8% | [@mdpi2024enhanced] |

: Literature baselines on UNSW-NB15 standard split. {#tbl-standard-baselines}

Our WNN targets for the standard split:

| Metric | Target | Stretch Goal | Basis |
|--------|--------|--------------|-------|
| **Accuracy** | $\geq$ 88% | $\geq$ 90% | Beat RF (87.2%) and XGBoost (87.3%) |
| **F1-Macro** | $\geq$ 87% | $\geq$ 89% | Match or beat classical ML (~87%) |
| **FPR** | $\leq$ 12% | $\leq$ 8% | Match classical ML; stretch = match BiLSTM |
| Multi-class (10 classes) | $\geq$ 85% (F1) | $\geq$ 88% (F1) | Novel benchmark (no WNN prior art) |

: Our WNN accuracy goals on the standard split. {#tbl-our-goals}

Matching RF/XGBoost baselines on F1-Macro ($\geq$ 87%) and FPR ($\leq$ 12%) would validate the architecture for IDS. **Beating them would be publishable** --- no prior WNN work reports results on the standard split.

## Random Split Goals (Secondary --- FWIW Comparison)

| Task | Target | Basis |
|------|--------|-------|
| Binary (UNSW-NB15, random 90/10) | $\geq$ 98.5% | Match FWIW [@susskind2023fwiw] |
| Binary (CICIDS2017) | $\geq$ 99% | Match Random Forest |
| Cross-dataset generalization | $\leq$ 5% degradation | Better than reported 8% gap |
| Online adaptation (concept drift) | $\leq$ 5% accuracy loss over 30 days | Novel benchmark |

## Efficiency Goals

| Metric | Target | Basis |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Model size | $\leq$ 1 KB | Competitive with FWIW (192 B) |
| FPGA LUTs | $\leq$ 2,000 | Beat PolyLUT-Add (1,649) |
| Inference latency | $\leq$ 10 ns | Match PolyLUT-Add (8 ns) |

# Infrastructure Reuse

A key advantage of the pivot: ~80% of our existing Rust+Metal pipeline transfers directly.

## Reuse Directly

| Component | Why it works for IDS |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Rust/Metal accelerator | RAM neuron eval is identical for any classification |
| GA/TS connectivity optimization | Feature selection $\cong$ bit selection |
| Per-cluster evaluator | Discriminative fitness for attack classes |
| Dashboard + experiment tracking | Change configs, reuse everything else |
| Overfitting monitor | Same framework, IDS metrics |

## Adapt

| Component | Changes needed | Effort |
|-----------|---------------|--------|
| Feature encoder | New `ThermometerEncoder` for packet features | ~1 day |
| Evaluation metrics | Add detection rate, FPR, per-class F1 | ~1 day |
| FlowConfig / ExperimentConfig | IDS-specific fields | ~1 day |
| Worker | IDS dataset loading + preprocessing | ~2 days |

## Build New

| Component | What | Effort |
|-----------|------|--------|
| Dataset pipeline | Download, preprocess, binary vectorize | ~2 days |
| Online learning module | Incremental train/untrain | ~3 days |
| RTL export | Python model $\rightarrow$ Verilog lookup tables | ~1 week |
| FPGA synthesis scripts | Vivado project and constraints | ~1 week |

# Implementation Roadmap

```
Phase A (Weeks 17-18): Datasets + Baselines
├── A1: Download UNSW-NB15, preprocess, thermometer encode
├── A2: Classical baselines (RF, XGBoost)
└── A3: WNN baselines (clone FWIW, BTHOWeN, DWN; reproduce)

Phase B (Weeks 19-21): Our WNN Classifier
├── B1: Adapt pipeline (dataset loader, encoder, metrics)
├── B2: Binary classification with GA/TS optimization
├── B3: Multi-class classification (10 classes)
└── B4: Cross-dataset generalization

Phase C (Weeks 22-23): Online Learning
├── C1: Incremental train/untrain
└── C2: Concept drift simulation (NSL-KDD novel attacks)

Phase D (Weeks 24-27): FPGA Prototype
├── D1: RTL generation from trained model
├── D2: Vivado synthesis + benchmarks
└── D3: End-to-end demo (pcap → classification)

Phase E (Weeks 28-30): Edge AI Pilot
├── E1: HAR dataset on microcontroller
└── E2: Battery-powered inference demo
```

# Risk Assessment

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|-----------|
| WNN accuracy $<$ 98.5% on binary | Low | High | FWIW already proved 98.5%; GA/TS should help |
| Multi-class poor for rare attacks | Medium | Medium | Cost-sensitive fitness, oversampling |
| No FPGA hardware available | Medium | Medium | Vivado simulation; cloud FPGA (AWS F1) |
| Online learning catastrophic forgetting | Medium | Medium | Sliding window, selective untraining |
| Thermometer encoding is bottleneck | Low | Low | Multiple variants available |

# What's Next

Phase A starts immediately. First task: download UNSW-NB15 and implement the feature preprocessing pipeline with thermometer encoding.
